places.name: Indus
facts: Rises in Tibet near Lake Manasarovar and enters India in Ladakh near Demchok.
Flows past Leh; its Indian tributaries are the Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej.
The Indus Waters Treaty (1960) gives India the eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) and Pakistan the western ones.

places.name: Zanskar
facts: Joins the Indus at Nimmu, west of Leh.
Its frozen gorge becomes the winter Chadar trek.

places.name: Shyok
facts: Rises at the Rimo glacier and receives the Nubra, fed by the Siachen glacier.
Called the "river of death"; it joins the Indus in Gilgit-Baltistan.

places.name: Jhelum
facts: Rises at the Verinag spring and flows through the Kashmir Valley, Srinagar and Wular lake.
Joins the Chenab at Trimmu in Pakistan.
Kishanganga (Neelum) joins it near Muzaffarabad.

places.name: Kishanganga
facts: Called the Neelum in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir.
The Kishanganga hydroelectric project diverts its water to the Jhelum basin (upheld by the Court of Arbitration, 2013).

places.name: Chenab
facts: Formed by the Chandra and Bhaga at Tandi in Lahaul.
The largest tributary of the Indus by volume.
The Chenab rail bridge near Reasi is the world’s highest railway arch bridge.

places.name: Ravi
facts: Rises in the Bara Bhangal area of the Dhauladhar and flows through the Chamba valley.
The Ranjit Sagar (Thein) dam is on the Ravi; it enters Pakistan near Amritsar and flows past Lahore.

places.name: Beas
facts: Rises at Beas Kund near the Rohtang pass and flows through the Kullu valley.
Pong dam (Maharana Pratap Sagar) is on the Beas; it joins the Sutlej at Harike.
The only Indus tributary that flows wholly within India.

places.name: Sutlej
facts: Rises near Rakshastal in Tibet and enters India at the Shipki La.
Bhakra Nangal dam (Gobind Sagar) and Nathpa Jhakri are on the Sutlej.
Joins the Beas at Harike and forms part of the India–Pakistan border.

places.name: Ghaggar
facts: A seasonal river that rises in the Shivalik hills and dies out in the Thar desert.
Often identified with the Vedic Saraswati; many Harappan sites (Kalibangan, Rakhigarhi) lie in its basin.

places.name: Luni
facts: Rises in the Pushkar valley of the Aravalli near Ajmer.
The only river of the Thar desert; its water turns saline below Balotra.
It does not reach the sea but ends in the marshes of the Rann of Kutch.

places.name: Sabarmati
facts: Rises in the Aravalli hills of Udaipur district, Rajasthan.
Flows past Gandhinagar and Ahmedabad (Sabarmati Ashram) into the Gulf of Khambhat.

places.name: Mahi
facts: Rises in the Vindhya range in Dhar district, Madhya Pradesh.
Crosses the Tropic of Cancer twice.
The Mahi Bajaj Sagar dam is at Banswara; it enters the Gulf of Khambhat.

places.name: Ganga
facts: Formed at Devprayag where the Bhagirathi meets the Alaknanda; enters the plains at Haridwar.
Meets the Yamuna at Prayagraj; flows past Kanpur, Varanasi and Patna.
India’s national river (2008) and the Ganga river dolphin its national aquatic animal (2009).
Divides at Farakka: the Padma flows into Bangladesh, the Bhagirathi–Hooghly to Kolkata.

places.name: Bhagirathi
facts: Rises at Gaumukh, the snout of the Gangotri glacier.
Tehri dam, India’s tallest, is on the Bhagirathi.
Considered the source stream of the Ganga.

places.name: Alaknanda
facts: Rises at the Satopanth and Bhagirath Kharak glaciers near Badrinath.
Its Panch Prayag: Vishnuprayag (Dhauliganga), Nandprayag (Nandakini), Karnaprayag (Pindar), Rudraprayag (Mandakini), Devprayag (Bhagirathi).
Carries more water than the Bhagirathi at Devprayag.

places.name: Yamuna
facts: Rises at the Yamunotri glacier on the Bandarpunch massif.
Flows past Delhi, Mathura and Agra and joins the Ganga at the Triveni Sangam, Prayagraj.
The longest tributary of the Ganga; the Chambal, Sind, Betwa and Ken join it from the south.

places.name: Hindon
facts: Rises in the Shivalik hills of Saharanpur district.
Flows past Ghaziabad and Noida into the Yamuna.

places.name: Chambal
facts: Rises in the Janapav hills near Mhow in the Vindhya.
Gandhi Sagar, Rana Pratap Sagar, Jawahar Sagar and the Kota barrage are on it.
Famous for its ravines (badlands) and the National Chambal Sanctuary for gharials.

places.name: Banas
facts: Rises in the Aravalli near Kumbhalgarh and flows entirely in Rajasthan.
The Bisalpur dam, which supplies Jaipur, is on the Banas.

places.name: Parbati
facts: A right-bank tributary of the Chambal draining the Malwa plateau.

places.name: Betwa
facts: Rises in the Vindhya near Bhopal and joins the Yamuna at Hamirpur.
Orchha stands on its banks; the Rajghat and Matatila dams are on it.
The Ken–Betwa link is India’s first river-interlinking project.

places.name: Ken
facts: Flows through Panna Tiger Reserve and Bundelkhand; famous for its shajar stones.
Joins the Yamuna at Chilla in Banda district.
Source river for the Ken–Betwa link.

places.name: Son
facts: Rises at Amarkantak and is the largest southern tributary of the Ganga.
Bansagar dam is on the Son; the Rihand joins it.
Joins the Ganga near Patna.

places.name: Gomti
facts: Rises at Gomat Taal near Madho Tanda, Pilibhit.
Lucknow and Jaunpur stand on the Gomti.
Joins the Ganga at Kaithi near Saidpur, Ghazipur.

places.name: Ramganga
facts: Rises in the Dudatoli hills of Uttarakhand and flows through Corbett National Park (Kalagarh dam).
Flows past Moradabad and Bareilly and joins the Ganga near Kannauj.

places.name: Sharda
facts: Called the Kali or Mahakali in the hills, where it forms the India–Nepal border.
The Mahakali Treaty (1996) covers the Pancheshwar project.
Joins the Ghaghara in Bahraich district.

places.name: Ghaghara
facts: Rises near Manasarovar as the Karnali and flows through Nepal.
Known as the Saryu at Ayodhya.
Joins the Ganga near Chhapra, Bihar.

places.name: Rapti
facts: Rises in Nepal and flows past Gorakhpur, causing frequent floods in eastern UP.
Joins the Ghaghara at Barhaj.

places.name: Gandak
facts: Called the Kali Gandaki in Nepal, where it cuts one of the world’s deepest gorges.
Enters India at Valmikinagar (Valmiki Tiger Reserve) and joins the Ganga opposite Patna.

places.name: Kosi
facts: Formed in Nepal by seven streams, including the Arun from Tibet.
Called the “Sorrow of Bihar” for its floods and shifting course.
Joins the Ganga near Kursela.

places.name: Damodar
facts: Rises in the Chota Nagpur plateau and flows east through a rift valley rich in coal.
Once the “Sorrow of Bengal”; the Damodar Valley Corporation (1948) was India’s first multipurpose river project.
Tilaiya, Konar, Maithon and Panchet dams are in its basin.

places.name: Hooghly
facts: A distributary of the Ganga, fed by the Farakka feeder canal.
Kolkata and Haldia ports lie on it.

places.name: Subarnarekha
facts: Rises near Ranchi; the Hundru falls are on it.
Flows past Jamshedpur and reaches the Bay of Bengal between West Bengal and Odisha.

places.name: Narmada
facts: Rises at Amarkantak and flows west through a rift valley between the Vindhya and Satpura.
The largest west-flowing river of the peninsula; forms an estuary at Bharuch.
Dhuandhar falls, Indira Sagar, Omkareshwar and Sardar Sarovar dams are on it.

places.name: Tapi
facts: Rises near Multai in the Satpura range (Betul district).
Flows west in a rift valley parallel to the Narmada; Surat stands at its mouth.
The Ukai dam is on the Tapi; the Purna is its main tributary.

places.name: Mandovi
facts: Rises at Bhimgad in Karnataka; Dudhsagar falls are on it.
Panaji stands on its estuary; the Mhadei water dispute involves Goa, Karnataka and Maharashtra.

places.name: Sharavathi
facts: Plunges 253 m at Jog Falls.
Linganamakki reservoir feeds the Sharavathi hydroelectric project; it meets the sea at Honnavar.

places.name: Netravati
facts: Rises near Kudremukh and reaches the sea at Mangaluru.

places.name: Periyar
facts: The longest river of Kerala, rising in the Sivagiri hills.
Mullaperiyar and Idukki dams are in its basin; Periyar Tiger Reserve surrounds its lake.
Reaches the sea near Kochi.

places.name: Bharathapuzha
facts: Kerala’s second-longest river; flows through the Palghat Gap and reaches the sea at Ponnani.

places.name: Mahanadi
facts: Rises in the Sihawa hills of Dhamtari district, Chhattisgarh.
Hirakud, one of the world’s longest earthen dams, is at Sambalpur.
Forms a large delta around Cuttack and reaches the sea near Paradip.

places.name: Brahmani
facts: Formed by the Sankh and South Koel at Vedvyas near Rourkela.
Meets the Baitarani near the sea at Dhamra; the Bhitarkanika mangroves lie in the combined delta.

places.name: Baitarani
facts: Rises in the Gonasika hills of Keonjhar.
Joins the Brahmani delta near Dhamra.

places.name: Godavari
facts: Rises at Trimbakeshwar near Nashik; the longest river of the peninsula (about 1,465 km).
Called the Dakshin Ganga; its basin is the largest in peninsular India.
Tributaries: Pravara, Manjra (right); Penganga, Wardha, Wainganga, Indravati, Sabari (left).
Polavaram project and the Dowleswaram barrage are near its delta.

places.name: Manjra
facts: Rises in the Balaghat range near Beed; Nizam Sagar dam is on it.

places.name: Wardha
facts: Rises in the Satpura range near Multai.
Joins the Wainganga to form the Pranhita.

places.name: Wainganga
facts: Rises in the Mahadeo hills of Seoni and flows through Pench.
With the Wardha it forms the Pranhita, which joins the Godavari at Kaleshwaram.

places.name: Indravati
facts: Rises in the Kalahandi hills of Odisha and flows through Bastar.
Chitrakote falls, the “Niagara of India”, are on it; Indravati Tiger Reserve lies along it.

places.name: Sabari
facts: Called the Kolab in Odisha; joins the Godavari at Kunavaram.

places.name: Krishna
facts: Rises at Mahabaleshwar in the Western Ghats.
Almatti, Srisailam and Nagarjuna Sagar dams and the Prakasam barrage at Vijayawada are on it.
Tributaries: Koyna, Ghataprabha, Malaprabha, Tungabhadra (right); Bhima, Musi, Munneru (left).

places.name: Koyna
facts: Flows south from Mahabaleshwar; the Koyna dam supplies one of India’s largest hydroelectric stations.
The 1967 Koyna earthquake is linked to reservoir-induced seismicity.
Joins the Krishna at Karad (Preeti Sangam).

places.name: Ghataprabha
facts: The Gokak falls are on the Ghataprabha.

places.name: Malaprabha
facts: Badami, Aihole and Pattadakal lie in its valley; joins the Krishna at Kudalasangama.

places.name: Bhima
facts: Rises at Bhimashankar; Pandharpur stands on it (as the Chandrabhaga).
The Ujani dam is on the Bhima; it joins the Krishna near Raichur.

places.name: Tungabhadra
facts: Formed by the Tunga and Bhadra at Koodli near Shivamogga.
Hampi lies on its bank; the Tungabhadra dam is at Hosapete.
Joins the Krishna near Kurnool.

places.name: Musi
facts: Hyderabad was founded on the Musi; Osman Sagar and Himayat Sagar are on its tributaries.

places.name: Penner
facts: Rises in the Nandi hills of Chikkaballapur, Karnataka.
Flows through the rain-shadow Rayalaseema and reaches the sea near Nellore.

places.name: Palar
facts: A seasonal river from the Nandi hills flowing past Vellore to the sea south of Chennai.

places.name: Kaveri
facts: Rises at Talakaveri in the Brahmagiri hills of Kodagu.
Krishna Raja Sagara and Mettur dams; Shivanasamudra and Hogenakkal falls; Srirangam island.
Tributaries: Hemavati, Kabini, Bhavani, Amaravati, Noyyal, Arkavathi.
Its delta is the “rice bowl” of Tamil Nadu; the Grand Anicut (Kallanai) dates from the 2nd century.

places.name: Kolidam
facts: The northern distributary of the Kaveri, branching at Srirangam.

places.name: Kabini
facts: Rises in Wayanad and separates Nagarhole from Bandipur; joins the Kaveri at T. Narasipura.

places.name: Bhavani
facts: Rises in the Silent Valley; the Bhavanisagar dam is on it.

places.name: Vaigai
facts: Rises in the Varusanad hills; Madurai stands on it.
Receives water diverted from the Periyar through the Mullaperiyar project.

places.name: Tamirabarani
facts: Tamil Nadu’s only perennial river, rising at Agasthyamalai; Tirunelveli stands on it.

places.name: Brahmaputra
facts: Rises at the Chemayungdung glacier near Manasarovar as the Yarlung Tsangpo.
Takes a great bend around Namcha Barwa and enters Arunachal as the Siang (Dihang).
Becomes the Brahmaputra near Sadiya where the Dibang and Lohit join; Majuli is its river island.
In Bangladesh it is the Jamuna and joins the Padma.

places.name: Siang
facts: The Yarlung Tsangpo becomes the Siang where it enters India at Gelling.

places.name: Dibang
facts: Joins near Sadiya; the Dibang multipurpose project is set to be India’s tallest dam.

places.name: Lohit
facts: Enters India from Tibet near Kibithu; Parshuram Kund is on it.
The Dhola–Sadiya (Bhupen Hazarika) bridge crosses it.

places.name: Subansiri
facts: The largest tributary of the Brahmaputra; rises in Tibet.
The Subansiri Lower project is one of India’s largest hydroelectric schemes.

places.name: Kameng
facts: Separates Pakke and Nameri tiger reserves; joins the Brahmaputra near Tezpur.

places.name: Manas
facts: Flows from Bhutan through Manas National Park, a World Heritage Site.

places.name: Dhansiri
facts: Rises at Laisang peak in Nagaland and flows past Golaghat.

places.name: Teesta
facts: Rises at the Tso Lhamo (Cholamu) lake in north Sikkim.
The lifeline of Sikkim; flows past Jalpaiguri into Bangladesh.
Sharing its water is a long-running India–Bangladesh issue.

places.name: Barak
facts: Rises in the Manipur hills near Senapati; Silchar stands on it.
In Bangladesh it splits into the Surma and Kushiyara, which form the Meghna.

places.name: Kaladan
facts: Flows from Mizoram through Myanmar to Sittwe.
The Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Project links Kolkata to Mizoram through Sittwe port.

places.name: Karakoram
facts: Trans-Himalayan range with K2 (8,611 m), India’s highest peak.
Holds the largest glaciers outside the polar regions, including Siachen, Baltoro and Biafo.

places.name: Ladakh Range
facts: Runs parallel to the Indus, north of Leh; Khardung La crosses it.

places.name: Zanskar Range
facts: Separates Zanskar and Ladakh from the Great Himalaya.

places.name: Great Himalaya
facts: The highest and most continuous range, average height about 6,000 m, with a granite core.
Holds Kangchenjunga, Nanda Devi and Kamet within India.

places.name: Pir Panjal
facts: The longest range of the Lesser Himalaya (Himachal).
Crossed by the Banihal pass, the Jawahar and Banihal–Qazigund tunnels and the Mughal Road.

places.name: Dhauladhar
facts: Lesser Himalayan range rising abruptly behind Dharamshala and the Kangra valley.

places.name: Shiwalik
facts: The outermost and youngest range, of unconsolidated river sediments.
Longitudinal valleys between it and the Lesser Himalaya are called duns (e.g. Dehradun).

places.name: Patkai
facts: Part of the Purvanchal hills on the India–Myanmar border.
The Pangsau pass and the Ledo (Stilwell) road cross it.

places.name: Mishmi Hills
facts: Where the Himalaya bends south into the Purvanchal; the Dibang and Lohit cut through.

places.name: Naga Hills
facts: Part of the Purvanchal; Saramati (3,826 m) is the highest peak.

places.name: Mizo Hills
facts: Southern Purvanchal; Phawngpui (Blue Mountain) is the highest point.

places.name: Garo Hills
facts: Western part of the Meghalaya plateau; Nokrek biosphere reserve.

places.name: Khasi Hills
facts: Central Meghalaya plateau; Shillong, Sohra (Cherrapunji) and Mawsynram lie here.

places.name: Jaintia Hills
facts: Eastern Meghalaya plateau, rich in coal and limestone.

places.name: Karbi Anglong Hills
facts: A detached block of the peninsular plateau in Assam, south of Kaziranga.

places.name: Aravalli
facts: One of the oldest fold mountains in the world, running about 700 km from Gujarat to Delhi.
Guru Shikhar (1,722 m) on Mount Abu is the highest point.
Separates the Thar desert from the Malwa and eastern Rajasthan.

places.name: Vindhya
facts: Escarpment north of the Narmada; the traditional divide of north and south India.
Continues east as the Bharner and Kaimur hills.

places.name: Kaimur
facts: Eastern part of the Vindhya, overlooking the Son valley.

places.name: Satpura
facts: Block mountains between the Narmada and Tapi rift valleys.
Dhupgarh (1,350 m) near Pachmarhi is the highest peak.

places.name: Mahadeo Hills
facts: Central part of the Satpura with Pachmarhi, Madhya Pradesh’s only hill station.

places.name: Maikal Range
facts: Eastern end of the Satpura; Amarkantak, the source of the Narmada and Son, is here.

places.name: Rajmahal Hills
facts: Basaltic hills at the north-eastern edge of the peninsular plateau, where the Ganga turns south.

places.name: Western Ghats
facts: A continuous escarpment along the west coast, about 1,600 km long.
A UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the world’s biodiversity hotspots.
Anamudi (2,695 m) is the highest peak.

places.name: Eastern Ghats
facts: Discontinuous hills cut by the Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri.
Jindhagada / Arma Konda (about 1,690 m) is the highest point.

places.name: Nilgiri Hills
facts: Where the Western and Eastern Ghats meet; Doddabetta (2,637 m) is the highest peak.
Ooty lies here; the Nilgiri biosphere reserve was India’s first (1986).

places.name: Anaimalai Hills
facts: South of the Palghat Gap; Anamudi, the highest peak of south India, is here.

places.name: Cardamom Hills
facts: Southern Western Ghats known for cardamom and pepper; Periyar Tiger Reserve lies here.

places.name: Palani Hills
facts: Eastern spur of the Western Ghats with the hill station of Kodaikanal.

places.name: Nallamala Hills
facts: Part of the Eastern Ghats; Srisailam and the Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve lie here.

places.name: Javadi Hills
facts: Eastern Ghats hills known for the Vainu Bappu observatory at Kavalur.

places.name: Shevaroy Hills
facts: Eastern Ghats hills with the hill station of Yercaud.

places.name: K2
facts: India’s highest peak and the world’s second highest.
Lies in the Karakoram in Gilgit-Baltistan (Indian territory under Pakistan’s occupation).

places.name: Kangchenjunga
facts: The world’s third-highest peak, on the Sikkim–Nepal border.
The highest peak in India’s administered territory; worshipped as Sikkim’s guardian deity.

places.name: Nanda Devi
facts: The highest peak lying entirely within India.
Surrounded by the Nanda Devi sanctuary, part of a World Heritage Site.

places.name: Kamet
facts: Second-highest peak of Garhwal, near the Tibet border.

places.name: Saltoro Kangri
facts: Highest peak of the Saltoro ridge, west of the Siachen glacier.

places.name: Trisul
facts: Three-peaked massif south-west of Nanda Devi.

places.name: Nun
facts: Highest peak of the Nun Kun massif, in the Zanskar range.

places.name: Reo Purgyil
facts: Highest peak of Himachal Pradesh, on the Tibet border above the Sutlej.

places.name: Kangto
facts: Highest peak of Arunachal Pradesh, on the border with Tibet.

places.name: Saramati
facts: Highest peak of Nagaland, on the India–Myanmar border.

places.name: Sandakphu
facts: Highest point of West Bengal, on the Singalila ridge; four of the five highest peaks are visible from it.

places.name: Phawngpui
facts: Highest peak of Mizoram.

places.name: Anamudi
facts: Highest peak of India south of the Himalaya, in Eravikulam National Park.

places.name: Doddabetta
facts: Highest peak of the Nilgiris, near Ooty.

places.name: Mullayanagiri
facts: Highest peak of Karnataka, in the Baba Budan hills of Chikkamagaluru.

places.name: Kalsubai
facts: Highest peak of Maharashtra.

places.name: Guru Shikhar
facts: Highest peak of the Aravalli, on Mount Abu.

places.name: Dhupgarh
facts: Highest peak of the Satpura and of Madhya Pradesh, near Pachmarhi.

places.name: Parasnath
facts: Highest peak of Jharkhand; Shikharji, a major Jain pilgrimage site.

places.name: Mahendragiri
facts: One of the highest peaks of the Eastern Ghats, in Gajapati district.

places.name: Saddle Peak
facts: Highest point of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, on North Andaman.

places.name: Barren Island
facts: India’s only active volcano, in the Andaman Sea.

places.name: Narcondam
facts: A dormant volcanic island, home of the endemic Narcondam hornbill.

places.name: Mount Everest
facts: The world’s highest peak, on the Nepal–China border.
Its height of 8,848.86 m was jointly announced by Nepal and China in 2020.

places.name: Makalu
facts: World’s fifth-highest peak, south-east of Everest.

places.name: Dhaulagiri
facts: The Kali Gandaki gorge separates it from Annapurna.

places.name: Annapurna
facts: The first eight-thousander to be climbed (1950).

places.name: Nanga Parbat
facts: Western anchor of the Himalaya, where the Indus bends south.
Lies in Gilgit-Baltistan.

places.name: Namcha Barwa
facts: Eastern anchor of the Himalaya; the Yarlung Tsangpo makes its great bend around it.

places.name: Mount Kailash
facts: Sacred to Hindus, Buddhists, Jains and Bon.
The Indus, Sutlej, Brahmaputra and Karnali rise nearby.

places.name: Karakoram Pass
facts: Historic caravan route between Ladakh and Yarkand in Xinjiang.

places.name: Khardung La
facts: Connects Leh with the Nubra and Shyok valleys and the route to Siachen.
Often signposted as 5,602 m; surveyed height is about 5,359 m.

places.name: Chang La
facts: On the road from Leh to Pangong Tso.

places.name: Tanglang La
facts: High pass on the Manali–Leh highway.

places.name: Zoji La
facts: Links the Kashmir valley with Dras and Kargil on the Srinagar–Leh highway (NH 1).
The Zoji La tunnel will give all-weather access to Ladakh.

places.name: Banihal Pass
facts: Crosses the Pir Panjal between Jammu and the Kashmir valley.
Bypassed by the Jawahar road tunnel and the Banihal–Qazigund road and rail tunnels.

places.name: Pir Panjal Pass
facts: Carries the Mughal Road between Poonch–Rajouri and Shopian.

places.name: Burzil Pass
facts: Old route from Srinagar to Gilgit across the Deosai plains.

places.name: Rohtang Pass
facts: Connects the Kullu valley with Lahaul and Spiti.
Bypassed by the Atal Tunnel (2020), the world’s longest highway tunnel above 3,000 m.

places.name: Baralacha La
facts: On the Manali–Leh road; the Bhaga and Chandra rivers rise near it.

places.name: Kunzum Pass
facts: Connects Lahaul with the Spiti valley.

places.name: Shipki La
facts: Where the Sutlej enters India from Tibet; a border trade point in Kinnaur.

places.name: Mana Pass
facts: Above Badrinath, one of the highest motorable passes, leading to Tibet.

places.name: Niti Pass
facts: Old trade route from Garhwal to Tibet.

places.name: Lipulekh Pass
facts: Near the India–Nepal–China trijunction; route of the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra.
Border trade with Tibet passes here.

places.name: Nathu La
facts: Connects Sikkim with the Chumbi valley of Tibet on the old Silk Route.
Border trade reopened in 2006; also a Kailash Mansarovar Yatra route.

places.name: Jelep La
facts: Old Kalimpong–Lhasa trade route through the Chumbi valley.

places.name: Bum La
facts: Border point north of Tawang; one of the India–China border personnel meeting points.

places.name: Sela Pass
facts: Links Tawang with the rest of India; the Sela tunnel (2024) gives all-weather access.

places.name: Diphu Pass
facts: Near the India–China–Myanmar trijunction at the eastern end of the McMahon Line.

places.name: Pangsau Pass
facts: On the Stilwell (Ledo) road to Myanmar across the Patkai hills.

places.name: Palghat Gap
facts: A 30–40 km wide gap between the Nilgiri and Anaimalai hills.
Carries the road and railway between Coimbatore and Kerala and lets monsoon winds reach Tamil Nadu.

places.name: Shencottah Gap
facts: Links Kollam with Tirunelveli and Madurai across the southern Western Ghats.

places.name: Thal Ghat
facts: Carries the Mumbai–Nashik road and railway over the Western Ghats.

places.name: Bhor Ghat
facts: Carries the Mumbai–Pune road and railway over the Western Ghats.

places.name: Khyber Pass
facts: Links Peshawar with Kabul through the Spin Ghar range; the classic invasion route into India.

places.name: Bolan Pass
facts: Links Quetta with the Indus plain through the Toba Kakar range.

places.name: Khunjerab Pass
facts: Carries the Karakoram Highway from Gilgit-Baltistan into Xinjiang.

places.name: Siachen Glacier
facts: About 76 km long, the longest glacier of the Karakoram.
The world’s highest battlefield; source of the Nubra river.

places.name: Gangotri Glacier
facts: About 30 km long; its snout, Gaumukh, is the source of the Bhagirathi.

places.name: Yamunotri Glacier
facts: On the Bandarpunch massif; source of the Yamuna.

places.name: Satopanth Glacier
facts: Source of the Alaknanda, with the Bhagirath Kharak glacier.

places.name: Pindari Glacier
facts: Kumaon glacier feeding the Pindar, which joins the Alaknanda at Karnaprayag.

places.name: Milam Glacier
facts: Source of the Goriganga in Kumaon.

places.name: Zemu Glacier
facts: The largest glacier of the Eastern Himalaya, at the foot of Kangchenjunga; feeds the Teesta.

places.name: Bara Shigri Glacier
facts: The largest glacier of Himachal Pradesh, feeding the Chandra river.

places.name: Baltoro Glacier
facts: One of the longest glaciers outside the polar regions; leads to K2.

places.name: Chemayungdung Glacier
facts: Source of the Yarlung Tsangpo (Brahmaputra), south-east of Manasarovar.

places.name: Deccan Plateau
facts: Triangular tableland between the Western and Eastern Ghats, sloping gently east.
Its north-west is covered by the Deccan Traps basalt, weathered into black (regur) cotton soil.

places.name: Malwa Plateau
facts: Basaltic plateau north of the Vindhya, drained by the Chambal and Betwa.
Indore, Ujjain and Bhopal lie on it.

places.name: Chota Nagpur Plateau
facts: The “mineral heartland” of India: coal, iron ore, mica, bauxite and uranium.
Ranchi and Hazaribagh plateaus; the Damodar flows through a rift valley here.

places.name: Meghalaya Plateau
facts: A detached part of the peninsular plateau, separated by the Garo–Rajmahal gap.
Its south face catches the monsoon: Mawsynram and Sohra are among the wettest places on Earth.

places.name: Bundelkhand
facts: Granite and gneiss upland between the Yamuna and the Vindhya; drought-prone.
Jhansi, Banda and Chitrakoot lie here; the Betwa and Ken drain it.

places.name: Baghelkhand
facts: Upland east of Bundelkhand around Rewa, between the Son and the Kaimur.

places.name: Karnataka Plateau
facts: Southern Deccan, divided into the hilly Malnad and the plains of Maidan.

places.name: Telangana Plateau
facts: Eastern Deccan of Archaean gneiss, drained by the Godavari and Krishna.

places.name: Dandakaranya
facts: Forested plateau of Bastar and Koraput drained by the Indravati.

places.name: Amarkantak Plateau
facts: Source of the Narmada and Son (and the Johila); a pilgrimage centre.
Part of the Achanakmar-Amarkantak biosphere reserve.

places.name: Changthang
facts: High, cold plateau of eastern Ladakh, home of the Changpa herders and Pashmina goats.
Pangong Tso and Tso Moriri lie here.

places.name: Thar Desert
facts: Lies west of the Aravalli; receives less than 150 mm of rain in the far west.
The Luni is its only large river; the Desert National Park protects the Great Indian Bustard.

places.name: Rann of Kutch
facts: A seasonal salt marsh: flooded in the monsoon, a white salt flat in winter.
The Great Rann borders Pakistan; the Little Rann shelters the Indian wild ass.
places.subtitle: Salt marsh

places.name: Indo-Gangetic Plain
facts: One of the world’s largest alluvial plains, built by the Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra.
Older alluvium is bhangar; newer floodplain alluvium is khadar.

places.name: Ganga–Yamuna Doab
facts: The fertile land between the Ganga and Yamuna, from Haridwar to Prayagraj.

places.name: Terai
facts: A marshy, forested belt south of the Bhabar where streams re-emerge.
Dudhwa, Pilibhit and Valmiki reserves protect its grasslands.

places.name: Bhabar
facts: A narrow belt of pebbles at the foot of the Shiwalik where streams disappear underground.

places.name: Punjab Plains
facts: Formed by the Indus tributaries; its doabs are Bist, Bari, Rechna, Chaj and Sind Sagar.

places.name: Brahmaputra Valley
facts: A long, narrow alluvial valley between the Himalaya and the Meghalaya plateau.
Rich in tea, with Kaziranga and Majuli along the river.

places.name: Barak Valley
facts: Southern Assam around Silchar, drained by the Barak.

places.name: Kashmir Valley
facts: A basin between the Pir Panjal and the Great Himalaya, drained by the Jhelum.
Its lake deposits (karewas) are known for saffron.

places.name: Kullu Valley
facts: The Beas valley between Mandi and Manali, the “valley of gods”.

places.name: Kangra Valley
facts: Below the Dhauladhar; known for tea and miniature painting.

places.name: Lahaul Valley
facts: Chandra–Bhaga valley north of the Rohtang pass.

places.name: Spiti Valley
facts: A cold-desert valley on the Tibet border; Key monastery and Pin Valley National Park.

places.name: Nubra Valley
facts: Valley of the Shyok and Nubra north of Khardung La, with Bactrian camels at Hunder.

places.name: Galwan Valley
facts: Aksai Chin border valley, site of the June 2020 India–China clash.

places.name: Doon Valley
facts: A longitudinal valley (dun) between the Shiwalik and the Lesser Himalaya, with Dehradun.

places.name: Narmada Valley
facts: A rift valley between the Vindhya and Satpura; the Narmada flows west along it.
places.subtitle: Rift valley

places.name: Damodar Valley
facts: A rift valley holding Gondwana coal: Jharia, Raniganj and Bokaro coalfields.
places.subtitle: Rift valley

places.name: Imphal Valley
facts: An oval basin in the Manipur hills with Loktak lake at its south.

places.name: Araku Valley
facts: Eastern Ghats valley known for coffee and the Borra caves.

places.name: Chumbi Valley
facts: A Tibetan wedge between Sikkim and Bhutan, reached by the Nathu La and Jelep La.

places.name: Konkan Coast
facts: Rocky, indented coast from Daman to Goa, with the Konkan Railway.

places.name: Kanara Coast
facts: Karnataka coast from Goa to Mangaluru, with waterfalls from the Ghats.

places.name: Malabar Coast
facts: Kerala coast with lagoons and backwaters (kayals) behind sand bars.
Historic spice coast: Kozhikode, where Vasco da Gama landed in 1498.

places.name: Coromandel Coast
facts: Tamil Nadu coast from Pulicat to Point Calimere.
Gets most of its rain from the north-east (retreating) monsoon in winter.

places.name: Northern Circars
facts: Andhra coast between the Krishna and Mahanadi deltas.

places.name: Utkal Coast
facts: Odisha coast with the Mahanadi delta and Chilika lake.

places.name: Kathiawar Peninsula
facts: Peninsula between the Gulfs of Kutch and Khambhat; the Gir forest and Girnar hills lie at its centre.

places.name: Sundarbans Delta
facts: The world’s largest delta, shared by India and Bangladesh.
Named after the sundari mangrove tree.

places.name: Mahanadi Delta
facts: Densely populated delta around Cuttack; one of the most cyclone-prone coasts.

places.name: Godavari Delta
facts: Rice bowl of Andhra Pradesh, with the Coringa mangroves.

places.name: Krishna Delta
facts: Joins with the Godavari delta; Kolleru lake lies between them.

places.name: Kaveri Delta
facts: The “rice bowl of Tamil Nadu” around Thanjavur.

places.name: Majuli
facts: One of the world’s largest river islands, in the Brahmaputra.
India’s first island district (2016), a centre of Vaishnavite satras.

places.name: Umananda
facts: Among the smallest inhabited river islands, in the Brahmaputra at Guwahati.

places.name: Andaman Islands
facts: Peaks of a submarine range continuing the Arakan Yoma.
Separated from the Nicobars by the Ten Degree Channel.

places.name: Nicobar Islands
facts: Southern group of the UT; Car Nicobar in the north, Great Nicobar in the south.

places.name: Great Nicobar
facts: Largest of the Nicobars; a UNESCO biosphere reserve.
Site of the Great Nicobar transshipment port and township project.

places.name: Swaraj Dweep
facts: Renamed in 2018; known for Radhanagar beach.

places.name: Shaheed Dweep
facts: Renamed in 2018, south of Swaraj Dweep.

places.name: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Dweep
facts: Former British headquarters off Port Blair, renamed in 2018.

places.name: North Sentinel Island
facts: Home of the Sentinelese, one of the world’s last uncontacted peoples; entry is prohibited.

places.name: Lakshadweep Islands
facts: Coral atolls on the Chagos–Laccadive ridge; 36 islands, about 10 inhabited.

places.name: Minicoy
facts: Southernmost island of Lakshadweep, between the Nine and Eight Degree Channels.

places.name: Rameswaram
facts: Linked to the mainland by the Pamban bridges, including India’s first vertical-lift sea bridge (2025).
Adam’s Bridge (Ram Setu), a chain of shoals, runs from here towards Sri Lanka.

places.name: Sriharikota
facts: Barrier island between Pulicat lake and the sea.
Satish Dhawan Space Centre, ISRO’s launch port, is here.

places.name: Abdul Kalam Island
facts: Missile test range off the Odisha coast, renamed in 2015.

places.name: Elephanta Island
facts: Island in Mumbai harbour with rock-cut Shaiva caves, a World Heritage Site.

places.name: Diu
facts: Island off the Kathiawar coast; part of the UT of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu.

places.name: Katchatheevu
facts: Islet in the Palk Strait ceded by India to Sri Lanka in 1974.

places.name: Kanyakumari
facts: Southern tip of mainland India, where the Arabian Sea, Indian Ocean and Bay of Bengal meet.
Vivekananda Rock Memorial and the Thiruvalluvar statue stand offshore.

places.name: Indira Point
facts: India’s southernmost point, on Great Nicobar.
Its lighthouse area subsided in the 2004 tsunami.

places.name: Point Calimere
facts: Where the Coromandel coast turns west; a Ramsar wildlife sanctuary for flamingos.

places.name: Dhanushkodi
facts: Tip of Rameswaram island, destroyed by the 1964 cyclone; closest point to Sri Lanka.

places.name: Adam’s Bridge
facts: A chain of limestone shoals between Pamban and Mannar island, separating the Palk Bay from the Gulf of Mannar.
places.subtitle: Chain of shoals

places.name: Arabian Sea
facts: North-western arm of the Indian Ocean between India and the Arabian peninsula.

places.name: Bay of Bengal
facts: The world’s largest bay; the Ganga, Brahmaputra, Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri drain into it.

places.name: Andaman Sea
facts: Lies east of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, bordered by Myanmar and Thailand.

places.name: Lakshadweep Sea
facts: Between Lakshadweep, Kerala and the Maldives.

places.name: Gulf of Kutch
facts: Home of India’s first marine national park; Kandla (Deendayal) and Mundra ports lie on it.
Has one of India’s highest tidal ranges, suitable for tidal energy.

places.name: Gulf of Khambhat
facts: Receives the Sabarmati, Mahi, Narmada and Tapi.
Very high tides; the Alang ship-breaking yard is on its western shore.

places.name: Gulf of Mannar
facts: A marine national park and biosphere reserve rich in coral reefs, seagrass and dugongs.
Separated from the Palk Bay by Adam’s Bridge.

places.name: Palk Bay
facts: Shallow bay between Tamil Nadu and northern Sri Lanka.

places.name: Palk Strait
facts: Separates Tamil Nadu from the Jaffna peninsula of Sri Lanka.
Too shallow for large ships (the Sethusamudram canal was proposed to fix this).

places.name: Ten Degree Channel
facts: Separates Little Andaman from Car Nicobar along the 10°N parallel.

places.name: Nine Degree Channel
facts: Separates Minicoy from the main Lakshadweep islands.

places.name: Eight Degree Channel
facts: Separates Minicoy (India) from the Maldives.

places.name: Duncan Passage
facts: Separates South Andaman from Little Andaman.

places.name: Coco Channel
facts: Separates North Andaman from Myanmar’s Coco Islands.

places.name: Great Channel
facts: Separates Great Nicobar from Sumatra (Indonesia).

places.name: Sir Creek
facts: A 96 km tidal estuary in the Rann of Kutch marshes, disputed between India and Pakistan.
places.subtitle: Tidal estuary

places.name: Siliguri Corridor
facts: A strip about 20–22 km wide linking the Northeast with the rest of India, between Nepal and Bangladesh.

places.name: Doklam
facts: A plateau at the India–Bhutan–China trijunction; site of the 2017 standoff.

places.name: Aksai Chin
facts: High cold desert in eastern Ladakh claimed by India and occupied by China.

places.name: Kalapani
facts: Area near the Lipulekh pass at the source of the Kali; claimed by Nepal.

places.name: Wular Lake
facts: One of Asia’s largest freshwater lakes, formed by tectonic activity and fed by the Jhelum.
A Ramsar site (1990).

places.name: Dal Lake
facts: Srinagar’s lake of houseboats and floating gardens (rad).

places.name: Pangong Tso
facts: A 134 km long endorheic brackish lake at about 4,225 m, about a third in India.
The Line of Actual Control crosses it; site of the 2020–21 standoff.

places.name: Tso Moriri
facts: High-altitude lake in Changthang; breeding ground of the bar-headed goose and black-necked crane.

places.name: Tso Kar
facts: Saline lake complex of Changthang, a Ramsar site since 2020.

places.name: Chandra Taal
facts: Crescent lake near the source of the Chandra, in Lahaul-Spiti.

places.name: Renuka Lake
facts: The largest natural lake of Himachal Pradesh, in Sirmaur.

places.name: Nainital
facts: A tectonic lake of the Kumaon; the “lake district of India”.

places.name: Loktak Lake
facts: The largest freshwater lake of the Northeast, known for floating phumdis.
Keibul Lamjao, the only floating national park, lies on it; on the Montreux Record.

places.name: Chilika Lake
facts: Asia’s largest brackish-water lagoon and India’s first Ramsar site (1981).
Winter home of migratory birds and of Irrawaddy dolphins; Nalabana is a bird sanctuary.

places.name: Pulicat Lake
facts: India’s second-largest brackish lagoon; Sriharikota separates it from the sea.

places.name: Kolleru Lake
facts: Large freshwater lake between the Godavari and Krishna deltas.

places.name: Vembanad Lake
facts: India’s longest lake and Kerala’s largest; Kochi port lies at its mouth.
Scene of the Nehru Trophy boat race; the Kuttanad below-sea-level farms border it.

places.name: Ashtamudi Lake
facts: Palm-shaped estuary near Kollam, the gateway to the backwaters.

places.name: Sasthamkotta Lake
facts: The largest freshwater lake of Kerala.

places.name: Sambhar Lake
facts: India’s largest inland saline lake and a major source of salt.

places.name: Pushkar Lake
facts: Sacred lake near Ajmer with the rare Brahma temple; famous camel fair.

places.name: Lonar Lake
facts: A saline lake in a meteorite impact crater in basalt, about 50,000 years old.

places.name: Hussain Sagar
facts: A 16th-century lake between Hyderabad and Secunderabad.

places.name: Sukhna Lake
facts: Man-made lake at the foot of the Shiwalik in Chandigarh.

places.name: Gurudongmar Lake
facts: One of the world’s highest lakes (about 5,150 m), in north Sikkim.

places.name: Tsomgo Lake
facts: Glacial lake on the road from Gangtok to Nathu La.

places.name: Manasarovar
facts: Sacred freshwater lake near Mount Kailash, at about 4,590 m.
Pilgrims reach it by the Lipulekh and Nathu La routes.

places.name: Rakshastal
facts: Saline lake west of Manasarovar; the Sutlej rises near it.

places.name: Harike Wetland
facts: Formed by the Harike barrage at the confluence of the Sutlej and Beas.
Source of the Indira Gandhi Canal that irrigates the Thar.

places.name: Deepor Beel
facts: Permanent freshwater lake in a former Brahmaputra channel near Guwahati.

places.name: Kanwar Taal
facts: Bihar’s first Ramsar site, an oxbow lake of the Gandak in Begusarai.

places.name: East Kolkata Wetlands
facts: Treats Kolkata’s sewage naturally through fisheries and farms.

places.name: Rudrasagar Lake
facts: Lake with the Neermahal water palace.

places.name: Nal Sarovar
facts: Gujarat’s largest wetland bird sanctuary.

places.name: Hokersar
facts: “Queen of wetlands” of Kashmir, near Srinagar.

places.name: Nawabganj Bird Sanctuary
facts: Ramsar site between Lucknow and Kanpur.

places.name: Sur Sarovar
facts: Ramsar site near Agra on the Yamuna.

places.name: Sultanpur National Park
facts: Bird sanctuary near Gurugram, a Ramsar site.

places.name: Devprayag
facts: The Bhagirathi and Alaknanda meet here to form the Ganga; the last of the Panch Prayag.

places.name: Rudraprayag
facts: The Mandakini, from Kedarnath, joins the Alaknanda.

places.name: Karnaprayag
facts: The Pindar joins the Alaknanda.

places.name: Nandprayag
facts: The Nandakini joins the Alaknanda.

places.name: Vishnuprayag
facts: The Dhauliganga joins the Alaknanda; the first of the Panch Prayag.

places.name: Triveni Sangam
facts: Meeting of the Ganga, the Yamuna and the mythical Saraswati at Prayagraj.
Site of the Kumbh and Maha Kumbh melas.

places.name: Tandi
facts: The Chandra and Bhaga meet to form the Chenab (Chandrabhaga) in Lahaul.

places.name: Nimmu
facts: The Zanskar joins the Indus west of Leh.

places.name: Sadiya
facts: Near here the Siang, Dibang and Lohit unite as the Brahmaputra.

places.name: Kaleshwaram
facts: The Pranhita joins the Godavari; site of the Kaleshwaram lift irrigation project.

places.name: Koodli
facts: The Tunga and Bhadra meet to form the Tungabhadra.

places.name: Pachnada
facts: Five rivers meet: the Yamuna, Chambal, Sind, Kwari and Pahuj.

places.name: Jog Falls
facts: The Sharavathi plunges 253 m in four streams: Raja, Rani, Roarer and Rocket.

places.name: Kunchikal Falls
facts: Often cited as India’s highest waterfall (about 455 m), on the Varahi.

places.name: Nohkalikai Falls
facts: India’s tallest plunge waterfall (about 340 m), near Sohra.

places.name: Dudhsagar Falls
facts: Four-tiered falls on the Mandovi on the Goa–Karnataka border.

places.name: Athirappilly Falls
facts: The largest waterfall of Kerala, on the Chalakudy river.

places.name: Chitrakote Falls
facts: The widest waterfall in India, the “Niagara of India”, on the Indravati.

places.name: Dhuandhar Falls
facts: The Narmada’s “smoke cascade” at Bhedaghat, below the marble rocks.

places.name: Hundru Falls
facts: The Subarnarekha falls about 98 m near Ranchi.

places.name: Shivanasamudra Falls
facts: Asia’s first hydroelectric station was built here in 1902.

places.name: Hogenakkal Falls
facts: Kaveri falls on carbonatite rocks, known for coracle rides.

places.name: Gokak Falls
facts: Horseshoe falls on the Ghataprabha.

places.name: Bhakra Nangal Dam
facts: Concrete gravity dam on the Sutlej forming the Gobind Sagar reservoir.
Called a “temple of resurgent India” by Nehru; serves Punjab, Haryana and Rajasthan.

places.name: Pong Dam
facts: Earth-fill dam on the Beas; its reservoir, Maharana Pratap Sagar, is a Ramsar site.

places.name: Ranjit Sagar Dam
facts: On the Ravi on the Punjab–J&K border.

places.name: Salal Dam
facts: Run-of-the-river project on the Chenab near Reasi.

places.name: Baglihar Dam
facts: Chenab project whose design was examined by a neutral expert under the Indus Waters Treaty (2007).

places.name: Tehri Dam
facts: India’s tallest dam (about 260 m), on the Bhagirathi.

places.name: Farakka Barrage
facts: Diverts Ganga water to the Hooghly to keep Kolkata port navigable.
Water sharing is governed by the India–Bangladesh Ganga Treaty (1996).

places.name: Rihand Dam
facts: Its reservoir, Govind Ballabh Pant Sagar, is one of India’s largest artificial lakes.
The Singrauli power hub surrounds it.

places.name: Matatila Dam
facts: On the Betwa near Lalitpur on the UP–MP border.

places.name: Gandhi Sagar Dam
facts: First of the Chambal valley dams, upstream of Rana Pratap Sagar and Jawahar Sagar.

places.name: Indira Sagar Dam
facts: Has India’s largest reservoir by volume, on the Narmada.

places.name: Sardar Sarovar Dam
facts: Concrete gravity dam on the Narmada at Kevadia; the Statue of Unity stands downstream.
Centre of the Narmada Bachao Andolan.

places.name: Ukai Dam
facts: The largest reservoir of Gujarat, on the Tapi.

places.name: Hirakud Dam
facts: One of the world’s longest earthen dams (about 25.8 km with dykes), on the Mahanadi.

places.name: Maithon Dam
facts: Damodar Valley Corporation dam on the Barakar, a Damodar tributary.

places.name: Koyna Dam
facts: Serves one of India’s largest hydroelectric complexes; the Shivsagar reservoir.

places.name: Almatti Dam
facts: Upper Krishna project in Karnataka.

places.name: Tungabhadra Dam
facts: At Hosapete; a joint project of Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh.

places.name: Srisailam Dam
facts: On the Krishna in the Nallamala hills.

places.name: Nagarjuna Sagar Dam
facts: One of the world’s largest masonry dams, on the Krishna.

places.name: Polavaram Project
facts: National project on the Godavari with a link canal to the Krishna.

places.name: Krishna Raja Sagara
facts: Dam on the Kaveri near Mysuru, designed by M. Visvesvaraya; Brindavan gardens.

places.name: Mettur Dam
facts: Its reservoir, Stanley Reservoir, is one of Tamil Nadu’s largest.

places.name: Grand Anicut
facts: Built by the Chola king Karikalan around the 2nd century CE; still in use.

places.name: Idukki Dam
facts: A double-curvature arch dam on the Periyar between the Kuravan and Kurathi hills.

places.name: Mullaperiyar Dam
facts: Built in 1895 in Kerala but operated by Tamil Nadu; the subject of a long dispute.

places.name: New Delhi
facts: Capital of India, inaugurated in 1931 and designed by Lutyens and Baker.

places.name: Amaravati
facts: Capital of Andhra Pradesh, on the Krishna; an ancient Satavahana Buddhist centre.

places.name: Itanagar
facts: Capital of Arunachal Pradesh; the Ita fort gives it its name.

places.name: Dispur
facts: Capital of Assam, a locality of Guwahati.

places.name: Patna
facts: Capital of Bihar on the Ganga; ancient Pataliputra, capital of the Mauryas.

places.name: Raipur
facts: Capital of Chhattisgarh; Nava Raipur is the planned administrative city.

places.name: Panaji
facts: Capital of Goa on the Mandovi estuary.

places.name: Gandhinagar
facts: Planned capital of Gujarat on the Sabarmati.

places.name: Chandigarh
facts: Le Corbusier’s planned city; capital of Punjab and Haryana and itself a Union Territory.

places.name: Shimla
facts: Capital of Himachal Pradesh and former summer capital of British India.

places.name: Ranchi
facts: Capital of Jharkhand on the Ranchi plateau; the Subarnarekha rises nearby.

places.name: Bengaluru
facts: Capital of Karnataka on the Mysore plateau; India’s technology capital.

places.name: Thiruvananthapuram
facts: Capital of Kerala; Vizhinjam port and the VSSC space centre are nearby.

places.name: Bhopal
facts: Capital of Madhya Pradesh, the “city of lakes”; the Bhimbetka shelters are nearby.

places.name: Mumbai
facts: Capital of Maharashtra and India’s financial capital, built on seven islands.

places.name: Imphal
facts: Capital of Manipur in the Imphal valley.

places.name: Shillong
facts: Capital of Meghalaya on the Khasi hills, the “Scotland of the East”.

places.name: Aizawl
facts: Capital of Mizoram, on a ridge of the Mizo hills.

places.name: Kohima
facts: Capital of Nagaland; the 1944 battle of Kohima; the Hornbill festival is held nearby.

places.name: Bhubaneswar
facts: Capital of Odisha, the “temple city”, planned by Otto Koenigsberger.

places.name: Jaipur
facts: Capital of Rajasthan, the “pink city”, a World Heritage city.

places.name: Gangtok
facts: Capital of Sikkim, on the road to Nathu La.

places.name: Chennai
facts: Capital of Tamil Nadu on the Coromandel coast; Marina beach.

places.name: Hyderabad
facts: Capital of Telangana on the Musi; the Charminar.

places.name: Agartala
facts: Capital of Tripura, close to the Bangladesh border; linked to Akhaura by rail.

places.name: Lucknow
facts: Capital of Uttar Pradesh on the Gomti; the city of the Nawabs of Awadh.

places.name: Dehradun
facts: Capital of Uttarakhand in the Doon valley; Gairsain is the summer capital.

places.name: Kolkata
facts: Capital of West Bengal on the Hooghly; capital of British India until 1911.

places.name: Sri Vijaya Puram
facts: Capital of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, renamed from Port Blair in 2024.
The Cellular Jail is here.

places.name: Daman
facts: Capital of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu.

places.name: Srinagar
facts: Summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir, on the Jhelum and Dal lake.

places.name: Jammu
facts: Winter capital of Jammu and Kashmir, on the Tawi.

places.name: Leh
facts: Capital of Ladakh near the Indus, at about 3,500 m.

places.name: Kavaratti
facts: Capital of Lakshadweep, on a coral atoll.

places.name: Puducherry
facts: Capital of the UT; former French colony (until 1954); Auroville is nearby.

places.name: Islamabad
facts: Capital of Pakistan at the foot of the Margalla hills.

places.name: Kabul
facts: Capital of Afghanistan on the Kabul river.

places.name: Kathmandu
facts: Capital of Nepal in the Kathmandu valley.

places.name: Thimphu
facts: Capital of Bhutan in the Wang Chu valley.

places.name: Dhaka
facts: Capital of Bangladesh on the Buriganga.

places.name: Naypyidaw
facts: Capital of Myanmar since 2006, replacing Yangon.

places.name: Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte
facts: Legislative capital of Sri Lanka; Colombo is the commercial capital.

places.name: Varanasi
facts: One of the world’s oldest living cities, on the left bank of the Ganga.
Sarnath, where the Buddha first preached, is nearby.

places.name: Prayagraj
facts: At the Triveni Sangam; hosts the Kumbh mela.

places.name: Agra
facts: Mughal capital on the Yamuna: Taj Mahal, Agra Fort and nearby Fatehpur Sikri.

places.name: Kanpur
facts: Industrial city on the Ganga, known for leather.

places.name: Ayodhya
facts: On the Saryu (Ghaghara); the Ram Mandir opened in 2024.

places.name: Gorakhpur
facts: On the Rapti; has one of the world’s longest railway platforms.

places.name: Jhansi
facts: Gateway to Bundelkhand; Rani Lakshmibai’s fort.

places.name: Mathura
facts: On the Yamuna; a centre of the Mathura school of Kushan sculpture.

places.name: Meerut
facts: Where the revolt of 1857 began.

places.name: Bareilly
facts: Rohilkhand city on the Ramganga.

places.name: Ahmedabad
facts: India’s first World Heritage city (2017), on the Sabarmati.

places.name: Surat
facts: On the Tapi estuary; a world centre of diamond cutting.

places.name: Bhuj
facts: Kutch town rebuilt after the 2001 earthquake.

places.name: Pune
facts: On the Deccan plateau, east of the Bhor Ghat.

places.name: Nagpur
facts: Near the geographical centre of India (Zero Mile Stone); famous for oranges.

places.name: Nashik
facts: On the Godavari near its source; hosts a Kumbh mela.

places.name: Indore
facts: Largest city of Madhya Pradesh, on the Malwa plateau.

places.name: Ujjain
facts: On the Kshipra; its meridian was the prime meridian of ancient Indian astronomy.
The Tropic of Cancer passes close to it.

places.name: Jabalpur
facts: On the Narmada; the marble rocks of Bhedaghat are nearby.

places.name: Kota
facts: On the Chambal; the Kota barrage.

places.name: Jodhpur
facts: The “blue city” on the edge of the Thar, below Mehrangarh fort.

places.name: Jaisalmer
facts: The “golden city” in the heart of the Thar; its fort is a World Heritage hill fort.

places.name: Udaipur
facts: The “city of lakes” in the Aravalli: Pichola and Fateh Sagar.

places.name: Amritsar
facts: Home of the Golden Temple; the Attari–Wagah border is nearby.

places.name: Haridwar
facts: Where the Ganga leaves the hills and enters the plains; hosts a Kumbh mela.

places.name: Madurai
facts: Temple city on the Vaigai: the Meenakshi Amman temple.

places.name: Coimbatore
facts: The “Manchester of south India”, at the eastern end of the Palghat Gap.

places.name: Mysuru
facts: Former capital of the Wodeyars; famous for its Dasara.

places.name: Kochi
facts: Queen of the Arabian Sea; port on the Vembanad backwaters.

places.name: Kozhikode
facts: Vasco da Gama landed near here (Kappad) in 1498.

places.name: Visakhapatnam
facts: HQ of the Eastern Naval Command; a natural harbour protected by the Dolphin’s Nose.

places.name: Vijayawada
facts: On the Krishna at the Prakasam barrage.

places.name: Guwahati
facts: Gateway to the Northeast on the Brahmaputra; the Kamakhya temple.

places.name: Dibrugarh
facts: The “tea city of India”; the Bogibeel rail-road bridge is nearby.

places.name: Silchar
facts: Main town of the Barak valley.

places.name: Tawang
facts: Home of India’s largest Buddhist monastery, birthplace of the 6th Dalai Lama.

places.name: Darjeeling
facts: Hill station famous for tea (a GI product) and the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway.

places.name: Siliguri
facts: Commercial hub in the Siliguri corridor.

places.name: Sohra
facts: Once the wettest place on Earth; living root bridges nearby.

places.name: Mawsynram
facts: Receives the highest average annual rainfall on Earth, about 11,800 mm.

places.name: Dras
facts: One of the coldest inhabited places in India; the Kargil War Memorial.

places.name: Kargil
facts: On the Suru river; the 1999 Kargil War.

places.name: Manali
facts: Head of the Kullu valley, below the Rohtang pass.

places.name: Jamshedpur
facts: India’s first planned industrial city, founded around the Tata steel plant (1907).

places.name: Dhanbad
facts: The “coal capital of India”, beside the Jharia coalfield.

places.name: Bhilai
facts: Steel plant built with Soviet help (1959).

places.name: Rourkela
facts: Steel plant built with West German help (1959).

places.name: Durgapur
facts: Steel plant built with British help (1959), on the Damodar.

places.name: Puri
facts: Seat of the Jagannath temple and the Rath Yatra.

places.name: Lhasa
facts: Capital of the Tibet Autonomous Region on the Lhasa river, a tributary of the Yarlung Tsangpo.

places.name: Deendayal Port
facts: A tidal port on the Gulf of Kutch, built after Partition to replace Karachi.
Handles the most cargo of India’s major ports.

places.name: Mundra Port
facts: India’s largest private port.

places.name: Mumbai Port
facts: A natural harbour, one of India’s oldest major ports.

places.name: Jawaharlal Nehru Port
facts: India’s busiest container port, across the harbour from Mumbai.

places.name: Mormugao Port
facts: Goa’s natural harbour, historically India’s main iron-ore export port.

places.name: New Mangalore Port
facts: Exports Kudremukh iron ore and handles petroleum.

places.name: Cochin Port
facts: A natural harbour on Willingdon Island with the Vallarpadam transshipment terminal.

places.name: Vizhinjam Port
facts: India’s first deep-water container transshipment port, near the international shipping lane (2025).

places.name: V. O. Chidambaranar Port
facts: On the Gulf of Mannar; famous for pearl fishing.

places.name: Chennai Port
facts: An artificial harbour, one of India’s oldest ports.

places.name: Kamarajar Port
facts: India’s first corporatised major port.

places.name: Visakhapatnam Port
facts: India’s deepest landlocked and protected port.

places.name: Paradip Port
facts: Near the Mahanadi mouth; exports iron ore and handles coal.

places.name: Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port
facts: India’s only major river port, on the Hooghly; Haldia is its dock system downstream.

places.name: Haldia
facts: Deep-draft dock complex of Kolkata port at the Haldi–Hooghly confluence.

places.name: Gwadar
facts: Pakistani port built with China as part of CPEC.

places.name: Chittagong
facts: Bangladesh’s main port; India has transit access to it.

places.name: Sittwe
facts: Myanmar port built by India for the Kaladan project.

places.name: Hambantota
facts: Sri Lankan port leased to a Chinese company in 2017.

places.name: Jim Corbett National Park
facts: India’s first national park (1936, as Hailey NP) where Project Tiger was launched in 1973.

places.name: Rajaji National Park
facts: Shiwalik park known for elephants, near Haridwar.

places.name: Valley of Flowers
facts: High-altitude alpine meadow; with Nanda Devi, a World Heritage Site.

places.name: Nanda Devi National Park
facts: Glacial basin around Nanda Devi; core of a UNESCO biosphere reserve.

places.name: Great Himalayan National Park
facts: World Heritage Site in Kullu, home of the western tragopan.

places.name: Pin Valley National Park
facts: Cold-desert park in Spiti; snow leopard and ibex.

places.name: Hemis National Park
facts: India’s largest national park, famous for snow leopards.

places.name: Dachigam National Park
facts: Last stronghold of the hangul (Kashmir stag).

places.name: Dudhwa National Park
facts: Terai park on the Nepal border; swamp deer (barasingha) and rhinos reintroduced in 1984.

places.name: Pilibhit Tiger Reserve
facts: Won the TX2 award (2020) for doubling its tiger numbers; on the Sharda.

places.name: Amangarh Tiger Reserve
facts: Buffer of Corbett in Bijnor district.

places.name: Ranipur Tiger Reserve
facts: Uttar Pradesh’s fourth tiger reserve (2022), in Chitrakoot district.

places.name: Katarniaghat Wildlife Sanctuary
facts: On the Girwa river; gharials and Gangetic dolphins.

places.name: National Chambal Sanctuary
facts: Tri-state sanctuary for the critically endangered gharial and the Gangetic dolphin.

places.name: Valmiki Tiger Reserve
facts: Bihar’s only tiger reserve, where the Gandak enters India.

places.name: Kaziranga National Park
facts: Home of two-thirds of the world’s one-horned rhinoceroses; a World Heritage Site.

places.name: Manas National Park
facts: World Heritage Site on the Bhutan border; pygmy hog and golden langur.

places.name: Nameri National Park
facts: On the Jia Bharali, adjoining Pakke.

places.name: Dibru-Saikhowa National Park
facts: Riverine park known for its feral horses.

places.name: Pakke Tiger Reserve
facts: Known for hornbill conservation.

places.name: Namdapha National Park
facts: The only park with four big cats: tiger, leopard, snow leopard and clouded leopard.

places.name: Keibul Lamjao National Park
facts: The world’s only floating national park, on Loktak lake; last home of the sangai deer.

places.name: Nokrek National Park
facts: Garo hills biosphere reserve, a gene pool of wild citrus.

places.name: Khangchendzonga National Park
facts: India’s first “mixed” World Heritage Site (2016).

places.name: Singalila National Park
facts: Red panda habitat on the Singalila ridge.

places.name: Buxa Tiger Reserve
facts: In the Dooars on the Bhutan border.

places.name: Sundarbans National Park
facts: The largest mangrove forest in the world; Royal Bengal tigers swim between islands.

places.name: Similipal National Park
facts: Known for melanistic (pseudo-melanistic) tigers; Barehipani falls.

places.name: Bhitarkanika National Park
facts: Mangroves of the Brahmani–Baitarani delta with India’s largest saltwater crocodile population.

places.name: Gahirmatha Marine Sanctuary
facts: The world’s largest mass-nesting (arribada) site of Olive Ridley turtles.

places.name: Palamau Tiger Reserve
facts: One of the first nine Project Tiger reserves (1973); Betla National Park.

places.name: Kanha National Park
facts: Saved the hard-ground barasingha; the setting of The Jungle Book.

places.name: Bandhavgarh National Park
facts: One of the highest tiger densities in India; home of the first white tigers found in the wild.

places.name: Pench National Park
facts: On the Pench river along the MP–Maharashtra border.

places.name: Panna National Park
facts: Tigers were successfully reintroduced after local extinction (2009).

places.name: Satpura National Park
facts: Includes Pachmarhi; part of a UNESCO biosphere reserve.

places.name: Kuno National Park
facts: Where cheetahs from Namibia and South Africa were reintroduced in 2022.

places.name: Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve
facts: Maharashtra’s oldest and largest national park.

places.name: Melghat Tiger Reserve
facts: In the Gavilgarh hills of the Satpura.

places.name: Sanjay Gandhi National Park
facts: A national park inside Mumbai with the Kanheri caves.

places.name: Ranthambore National Park
facts: Tigers among the ruins of Ranthambore fort, where the Aravalli meets the Vindhya.

places.name: Sariska Tiger Reserve
facts: Lost all its tigers by 2005; the first successful tiger relocation followed.

places.name: Keoladeo National Park
facts: A man-made wetland, once the winter home of the Siberian crane.

places.name: Desert National Park
facts: Last stronghold of the Great Indian Bustard; fossil park at Akal.

places.name: Mukundra Hills Tiger Reserve
facts: Between the Chambal and Kali Sindh near Kota.

places.name: Gir National Park
facts: The only natural home of the Asiatic lion.

places.name: Marine National Park
facts: India’s first marine national park (1982), in the Gulf of Kutch.

places.name: Wild Ass Sanctuary
facts: Little Rann of Kutch; last home of the Indian wild ass (khur).

places.name: Velavadar Blackbuck National Park
facts: Grassland park for blackbuck on the Gulf of Khambhat.

places.name: Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve
facts: India’s largest tiger reserve, in the Nallamala hills.

places.name: Indravati National Park
facts: Home of the wild water buffalo.

places.name: Achanakmar Tiger Reserve
facts: Part of the Achanakmar-Amarkantak biosphere reserve.

places.name: Nagarhole National Park
facts: Also called Rajiv Gandhi NP; the Kabini separates it from Bandipur.

places.name: Bandipur National Park
facts: Part of the Nilgiri biosphere reserve, with India’s largest tiger and elephant populations nearby.

places.name: Kudremukh National Park
facts: Shola grasslands where the Tunga, Bhadra and Netravati rise.

places.name: Mudumalai National Park
facts: Where the Nilgiris meet the Mysore plateau; the Theppakadu elephant camp.

places.name: Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve
facts: India’s first biosphere reserve (1986), spanning three states.

places.name: Anamalai Tiger Reserve
facts: In the Anaimalai hills south of the Palghat Gap.

places.name: Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve
facts: India’s first marine biosphere reserve (1989); dugongs and coral islands.

places.name: Kalakkad-Mundanthurai Tiger Reserve
facts: Part of the Agasthyamalai biosphere reserve; the Tamirabarani rises here.

places.name: Periyar Tiger Reserve
facts: Around the Mullaperiyar reservoir at Thekkady, in the Cardamom hills.

places.name: Silent Valley National Park
facts: Undisturbed tropical evergreen forest saved from a dam by a 1970s movement.
Home of the lion-tailed macaque; the Kunthipuzha flows through it.

places.name: Eravikulam National Park
facts: Home of the Nilgiri tahr; Anamudi lies within it; neelakurinji blooms every 12 years.

places.name: Mahatma Gandhi Marine National Park
facts: Coral reefs off South Andaman.

places.name: Taj Mahal
facts: Shah Jahan’s marble mausoleum on the Yamuna (World Heritage 1983).

places.name: Fatehpur Sikri
facts: Akbar’s red-sandstone capital with the Buland Darwaza.

places.name: Sarnath
facts: Where the Buddha gave his first sermon; its Ashokan lion capital is India’s national emblem.

places.name: Kushinagar
facts: Where the Buddha attained mahaparinirvana.

places.name: Red Fort
facts: Shah Jahan’s fort in Shahjahanabad; the Prime Minister speaks here on Independence Day.

places.name: Qutub Minar
facts: Begun by Qutb-ud-din Aibak; the iron pillar stands in its complex.

places.name: Khajuraho
facts: Chandela temples in the Nagara style (c. 950–1050).

places.name: Sanchi Stupa
facts: Buddhist stupa begun by Ashoka.

places.name: Bhimbetka
facts: Rock shelters with paintings from the Palaeolithic onwards, in the Vindhya.

places.name: Ajanta Caves
facts: Buddhist caves with celebrated murals (2nd century BCE–6th century CE).

places.name: Ellora Caves
facts: Buddhist, Hindu and Jain caves, including the monolithic Kailasa temple.

places.name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus
facts: Victorian Gothic railway station in Mumbai.

places.name: Raigad Fort
facts: Shivaji’s capital; part of the Maratha Military Landscapes (World Heritage 2025).

places.name: Hampi
facts: Ruins of Vijayanagara on the Tungabhadra.

places.name: Pattadakal
facts: Chalukyan temples blending Nagara and Dravida styles.

places.name: Belur
facts: Hoysala temple; the Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas became World Heritage in 2023.

places.name: Konark Sun Temple
facts: 13th-century chariot-shaped temple to Surya, the “Black Pagoda”.

places.name: Mahabalipuram
facts: Pallava rathas and the Shore Temple.

places.name: Brihadisvara Temple
facts: Built by Rajaraja Chola I at Thanjavur; part of the Great Living Chola Temples.

places.name: Ramappa Temple
facts: Kakatiya temple, a World Heritage Site since 2021.

places.name: Rani ki Vav
facts: Stepwell at Patan on the Saraswati.

places.name: Dholavira
facts: Harappan city on Khadir island in the Rann of Kutch (World Heritage 2021).

places.name: Lothal
facts: Harappan port with one of the world’s oldest known dockyards.

places.name: Rakhigarhi
facts: The largest known Harappan site in India, in the Ghaggar basin.

places.name: Kalibangan
facts: Harappan site with the earliest ploughed field.

places.name: Chittorgarh Fort
facts: One of the Hill Forts of Rajasthan; Vijay Stambha.

places.name: Jantar Mantar
facts: Astronomical observatory built by Sawai Jai Singh II.

places.name: Mahabodhi Temple
facts: At Bodh Gaya, where the Buddha attained enlightenment.

places.name: Nalanda
facts: Ruins of the ancient university (5th–12th century).

places.name: Santiniketan
facts: Tagore’s university town, World Heritage in 2023.

places.name: Moidams of Charaideo
facts: Ahom royal burial mounds, World Heritage in 2024.

places.name: Churches of Goa
facts: Basilica of Bom Jesus in Old Goa, with the relics of St Francis Xavier.

places.name: Statue of Unity
facts: The world’s tallest statue (182 m), of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

places.name: Kedarnath
facts: Jyotirlinga temple at the head of the Mandakini valley.

places.name: Badrinath
facts: Char Dham shrine on the Alaknanda, near the Mana pass.

places.name: Pacific Ocean
facts: The largest and deepest ocean, covering about a third of the Earth.
Ringed by the “Ring of Fire” of volcanoes and trenches.

places.name: Atlantic Ocean
facts: The second-largest ocean; the Mid-Atlantic Ridge runs down its centre.

places.name: Indian Ocean
facts: The third-largest ocean and the only one named after a country.
Its monsoon winds reverse with the seasons.

places.name: Mediterranean Sea
facts: Nearly enclosed sea linked to the Atlantic by the Strait of Gibraltar and to the Red Sea by the Suez Canal.

places.name: Red Sea
facts: A young rift sea between Africa and Arabia, among the saltiest seas.

places.name: Black Sea
facts: Linked to the Mediterranean through the Bosporus and Dardanelles; the Danube drains into it.

places.name: South China Sea
facts: Contested sea with the Spratly and Paracel islands; a key trade route.

places.name: Caribbean Sea
facts: Bounded by the Greater and Lesser Antilles and Central America.

places.name: North Sea
facts: Shallow sea with the Dogger Bank fishing ground and oil and gas fields.

places.name: Baltic Sea
facts: Brackish, nearly enclosed sea of northern Europe.

places.name: Sargasso Sea
facts: The only sea with no coastline, bounded by ocean currents; named after sargassum seaweed.

places.name: Mariana Trench
facts: The deepest part of the oceans; the Challenger Deep is about 10,935 m deep.
places.subtitle: Ocean trench

places.name: Persian Gulf
facts: Holds about half the world’s proven oil reserves; exits through the Strait of Hormuz.

places.name: Gulf of Aden
facts: Between Yemen and Somalia; linked to the Red Sea by the Bab-el-Mandeb.

places.name: Gulf of Mexico
facts: The Gulf Stream begins here; the Mississippi drains into it.

places.name: Gulf of Guinea
facts: The Equator and the Prime Meridian cross in it.

places.name: Hudson Bay
facts: Huge inland sea of Canada, frozen for much of the year.

places.name: Gulf of Oman
facts: Links the Arabian Sea with the Strait of Hormuz.

places.name: Gulf of Thailand
facts: Shallow arm of the South China Sea.

places.name: Bay of Biscay
facts: Stormy bay between France and Spain.

places.name: Strait of Hormuz
facts: The world’s most important oil chokepoint, between Iran and Oman’s Musandam.

places.name: Strait of Malacca
facts: Busiest shipping lane between the Indian and Pacific Oceans, between Malaysia and Sumatra.

places.name: Bab-el-Mandeb
facts: “Gate of Tears” between Yemen and Djibouti, linking the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden.

places.name: Strait of Gibraltar
facts: Separates Europe (Spain) from Africa (Morocco); about 14 km wide.

places.name: Bosporus
facts: Divides Istanbul between Europe and Asia; links the Black Sea with the Sea of Marmara.

places.name: Dardanelles
facts: Links the Sea of Marmara with the Aegean; the Gallipoli campaign (1915).

places.name: Bering Strait
facts: Separates Asia from North America; the International Date Line runs through it.

places.name: Strait of Dover
facts: Narrowest part of the English Channel; the Channel Tunnel runs beneath it.

places.name: Sunda Strait
facts: Between Java and Sumatra; the Krakatoa volcano lies in it.

places.name: Lombok Strait
facts: Deep strait along the Wallace Line between Bali and Lombok.

places.name: Taiwan Strait
facts: Separates Taiwan from mainland China.

places.name: Strait of Magellan
facts: Navigable route around South America, north of Tierra del Fuego.

places.name: Drake Passage
facts: Between Cape Horn and Antarctica; the Antarctic Circumpolar Current flows through it.

places.name: Mozambique Channel
facts: Separates Madagascar from mainland Africa.

places.name: Cook Strait
facts: Separates the North and South Islands of New Zealand.

places.name: Bass Strait
facts: Separates Tasmania from mainland Australia.

places.name: Suez Canal
facts: Opened in 1869; a sea-level canal with no locks linking the Mediterranean and the Red Sea.
Shortens the Europe–India voyage by avoiding the Cape of Good Hope.

places.name: Panama Canal
facts: Opened in 1914; uses locks and the Gatun lake to link the Atlantic and Pacific.

places.name: Kiel Canal
facts: Links the North Sea with the Baltic across Germany; one of the busiest artificial waterways.

places.name: Himalaya
facts: The world’s highest range, raised by the collision of India with Asia.

places.name: Alps
facts: Young fold mountains of Europe; Mont Blanc is the highest peak.

places.name: Andes
facts: The world’s longest continental range (about 7,000 km); Aconcagua is its highest peak.

places.name: Rocky Mountains
facts: Western North American range forming the continental divide.

places.name: Atlas Mountains
facts: Fold mountains of north-west Africa separating the Mediterranean coast from the Sahara.

places.name: Ural Mountains
facts: Old range traditionally dividing Europe from Asia.

places.name: Caucasus
facts: Between the Black and Caspian seas; Elbrus is the highest peak.

places.name: Appalachian Mountains
facts: Old, worn-down range of eastern North America rich in coal.

places.name: Great Dividing Range
facts: Eastern Australian range separating the coast from the interior.

places.name: Drakensberg
facts: Basalt escarpment of southern Africa.

places.name: Hindu Kush
facts: Western extension of the Himalayan system into Afghanistan.

places.name: Tian Shan
facts: “Celestial mountains” of Central Asia.

places.name: Kunlun Mountains
facts: Northern rim of the Tibetan plateau.

places.name: Pamir
facts: The “roof of the world”, a knot where the Himalaya, Karakoram, Hindu Kush, Kunlun and Tian Shan meet.

places.name: Pyrenees
facts: Separates the Iberian peninsula from France.

places.name: Zagros Mountains
facts: Fold mountains of Iran with rich oil fields at their foot.

places.name: Carpathian Mountains
facts: Arc-shaped range of central and eastern Europe.

places.name: Aconcagua
facts: The highest peak outside Asia, in the Andes.

places.name: Denali
facts: The highest peak of North America, in Alaska.

places.name: Kilimanjaro
facts: Africa’s highest peak, a dormant volcano near the Equator with shrinking glaciers.

places.name: Mount Elbrus
facts: The highest peak of Europe, a dormant volcano in the Caucasus.

places.name: Mont Blanc
facts: The highest peak of the Alps.

places.name: Puncak Jaya
facts: The highest peak of Oceania, on New Guinea.

places.name: Mount Kosciuszko
facts: The highest peak of mainland Australia.

places.name: Mount Kenya
facts: Africa’s second-highest peak, an extinct volcano on the Equator.

places.name: Chimborazo
facts: Its summit is the point farthest from the Earth’s centre, because of the equatorial bulge.

places.name: Mount Fuji
facts: Japan’s highest peak, an active stratovolcano.

places.name: Mount Etna
facts: Europe’s most active volcano, on Sicily.

places.name: Mount Vesuvius
facts: Buried Pompeii and Herculaneum in 79 CE.

places.name: Krakatoa
facts: Its 1883 eruption was heard thousands of kilometres away.

places.name: Mauna Loa
facts: The largest active volcano on Earth by volume, a shield volcano over the Hawaii hotspot.

places.name: Cotopaxi
facts: One of the world’s highest active volcanoes.

places.name: Nile
facts: Often listed as the world’s longest river (about 6,650 km).
The White Nile (from Lake Victoria) and the Blue Nile (from Lake Tana) meet at Khartoum.
The Aswan High Dam forms Lake Nasser.

places.name: Amazon
facts: The largest river by discharge, about a fifth of all river water reaching the oceans.
Rises in the Peruvian Andes and crosses Brazil to the Atlantic.

places.name: Yangtze
facts: Asia’s longest river; the Three Gorges Dam is the world’s largest power station.

places.name: Huang He
facts: Carries loess silt; called “China’s sorrow” for its floods.

places.name: Mississippi
facts: With the Missouri, North America’s largest river system; ends in a bird’s-foot delta.

places.name: Congo
facts: Crosses the Equator twice; the deepest river in the world.

places.name: Niger
facts: Flows in a great boomerang past Timbuktu; forms an inland delta in Mali.

places.name: Zambezi
facts: Victoria Falls and the Kariba and Cahora Bassa dams are on it.

places.name: Mekong
facts: Flows through six countries; the Tonle Sap reverses its flow in the monsoon.

places.name: Danube
facts: Flows through ten countries, more than any other river; Vienna, Budapest and Belgrade stand on it.

places.name: Rhine
facts: Europe’s busiest waterway, from the Swiss Alps to Rotterdam.

places.name: Volga
facts: Europe’s longest river; drains into the Caspian Sea.

places.name: Ob
facts: Siberian river flowing north to the Kara Sea.

places.name: Yenisei
facts: The largest river system flowing into the Arctic Ocean.

places.name: Lena
facts: Siberian river flowing through permafrost to the Laptev Sea.

places.name: Amur
facts: Forms much of the Russia–China border.

places.name: Tigris
facts: With the Euphrates it enclosed Mesopotamia; Baghdad stands on it.

places.name: Euphrates
facts: Joins the Tigris to form the Shatt al-Arab, which enters the Persian Gulf.

places.name: Murray
facts: Australia’s longest river; the Murray–Darling basin is its farm belt.

places.name: Orinoco
facts: Drains the Llanos of Venezuela and Colombia.

places.name: Paraná
facts: The Itaipu dam on the Brazil–Paraguay border is one of the world’s largest.

places.name: St. Lawrence
facts: Outlet of the Great Lakes; the St. Lawrence Seaway lets ships reach the interior.

places.name: Colorado
facts: Carved the Grand Canyon; the Hoover Dam forms Lake Mead.

places.name: Mackenzie
facts: Canada’s longest river, flowing to the Arctic Ocean.

places.name: Limpopo
facts: Crosses the Tropic of Capricorn twice.

places.name: Jordan
facts: Flows through the Sea of Galilee into the Dead Sea.

places.name: Caspian Sea
facts: The world’s largest lake by area, saline and below sea level.

places.name: Lake Superior
facts: The largest freshwater lake by area; one of the Great Lakes.

places.name: Lake Baikal
facts: The world’s deepest (about 1,640 m) and oldest lake; holds about a fifth of unfrozen fresh surface water.

places.name: Lake Victoria
facts: Africa’s largest lake; source of the White Nile.

places.name: Lake Tanganyika
facts: The world’s longest freshwater lake, in the Great Rift Valley.

places.name: Lake Malawi
facts: Rift valley lake with hundreds of endemic cichlid fish.

places.name: Lake Titicaca
facts: The highest navigable lake (about 3,810 m), on the Altiplano.

places.name: Aral Sea
facts: Shrank drastically after the Amu Darya and Syr Darya were diverted for cotton.

places.name: Dead Sea
facts: Its shore is the lowest land on Earth, about 430 m below sea level.

places.name: Great Salt Lake
facts: Saline remnant of the ice-age Lake Bonneville.

places.name: Lake Chad
facts: A shallow Sahel lake that has shrunk dramatically since the 1960s.

places.name: Lake Ladoga
facts: Europe’s largest lake, near St Petersburg.

places.name: Lake Balkhash
facts: Freshwater in the west and saline in the east.

places.name: Lake Eyre
facts: Australia’s lowest point; usually a dry salt pan.

places.name: Sahara
facts: The largest hot desert, covering most of North Africa.

places.name: Arabian Desert
facts: Its Rub’ al Khali (Empty Quarter) is the largest continuous sand desert.

places.name: Gobi Desert
facts: A cold rain-shadow desert of Mongolia and China.

places.name: Kalahari Desert
facts: A semi-arid sandy savanna; home of the San people.

places.name: Namib Desert
facts: Coastal fog desert, among the oldest on Earth, caused by the cold Benguela current.

places.name: Atacama Desert
facts: The driest non-polar desert, caused by the cold Humboldt current; rich in copper and nitrates.

places.name: Great Victoria Desert
facts: Australia’s largest desert.

places.name: Taklamakan Desert
facts: Sandy desert of the Tarim basin, skirted by the Silk Road oases.

places.name: Patagonian Desert
facts: Cold rain-shadow desert east of the Andes.

places.name: Tibetan Plateau
facts: The highest and largest plateau, average height over 4,500 m; the “Third Pole”.

places.name: Ethiopian Highlands
facts: The “roof of Africa”; the Blue Nile rises at Lake Tana.

places.name: Altiplano
facts: High Andean plateau with Lake Titicaca and the Uyuni salt flat.

places.name: Anatolian Plateau
facts: Central plateau of Türkiye.

places.name: Colorado Plateau
facts: Layered plateau cut by the Grand Canyon.

places.name: Brazilian Highlands
facts: Ancient plateau of eastern Brazil with the Cerrado savanna.

places.name: Prairies
facts: Temperate grasslands of North America, the “wheat basket of the world”.

places.name: Pampas
facts: Temperate grasslands of Argentina known for cattle and wheat.

places.name: Steppes
facts: Temperate grasslands of Eurasia.

places.name: Veld
facts: Temperate grasslands of South Africa.

places.name: Downs
facts: Temperate grasslands of Australia, famed for merino sheep.

places.name: Llanos
facts: Tropical grasslands of the Orinoco basin.

places.name: Campos
facts: Tropical grasslands of the Brazilian Highlands.

places.name: Serengeti
facts: Savanna famous for the annual wildebeest migration.

places.name: Great Rift Valley
facts: A continental rift from the Red Sea to Mozambique, with deep lakes and volcanoes.

places.name: Grand Canyon
facts: Gorge up to 1.8 km deep carved by the Colorado river.

places.name: Death Valley
facts: The lowest and hottest place in North America.

places.name: Great Barrier Reef
facts: The world’s largest coral reef system, off Queensland; threatened by bleaching.
places.subtitle: Coral reef

places.name: Amazon Rainforest
facts: The largest tropical rainforest, with about a tenth of the world’s species.

places.name: Sahel
facts: Semi-arid belt south of the Sahara, facing desertification; the Great Green Wall is planted across it.

places.name: Horn of Africa
facts: Peninsula of north-east Africa guarding the Bab-el-Mandeb.

places.name: Golden Triangle
facts: Where Myanmar, Laos and Thailand meet on the Mekong; notorious for opium.

places.name: Golden Crescent
